findings.title: The new downsize definition replaces the width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature, so this second definition replaces the existing downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) method. Calls using four arguments now treat max_height as the options hash and fail when optimize accesses opts[:allow_animation]; calls supplying a fifth options argument fail with ArgumentError. Preserve the previously supported width/height form in a single compatible implementation.

findings.title: Reopen the tempfile after in-place optimization
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize calls ImageOptim.optimize_image!, which can replace the file at its pathname with an optimized file. The already-open tempfile then still references the old inode. Subsequent tempfile.size checks can remain stuck at an earlier size, and the filesize passed to Upload.create_for can differ from the resized file on disk. This can reject an image that was successfully reduced below the limit or record an incorrect filesize. Reopen the resulting file before checking its size and creating the upload, or resize into a separate tempfile.

findings.title: Percentage geometry is unsupported by the animated GIF resizer
findings.body: When allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled and the GIF tempfile has a .gif extension, downsize selects the animated implementation, which emits gifsicle --resize-fit 80%. That option requires width/height geometry rather than a percentage, so all five attempts fail and the oversized animated GIF remains above the upload limit. Use a GIF scaling operation or calculate explicit target dimensions.

findings.title: Do not impose the image input ceiling on attachments
findings.body: This hard-coded 10 MiB limit applies to attachments as well as images, replacing the configured max_attachment_size_kb limit even though attachments are not downsized. A site configured to permit attachments larger than 10 MiB now has otherwise-valid uploads rejected by the browser before they reach the server. Retain the configured attachment limit and apply the preprocessing ceiling only to images.
